issues.legal_issue: The yearly-lease presumption for a manufacturing tenancy does not apply to an oral lease that was not created by a registered instrument, so the challenged fifteen-day termination notice was not invalid on that ground.
material_facts: The dispute arose in an appeal in an eviction suit, and the tenant challenged the termination notice as too short.
The tenancy was created by oral agreement, and no registered written lease existed.
The tenant asserted that the premises were leased for manufacturing and that the tenancy therefore required six months’ notice.
Receipt of the fifteen-day termination notice was not disputed.
issues.conclusion: The statutory presumption of a year-to-year tenancy did not apply because the oral lease was not a valid year-to-year lease; the challenge to the fifteen-day notice therefore failed, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, is a rule of construction that determines the duration of a valid lease when the parties have not otherwise agreed; it does not itself create a valid year-to-year lease. Under Section 107, a lease from year to year, for a term exceeding one year, or reserving yearly rent must be made by registered instrument. The Court applied Ram Kumar Das v. Jagdish Chandra Deo, Dhabal Dev, which held that the rule of construction applies where there is no period agreed but requires a valid contract, and Shri Janki Devi Bhagat Trust, Agra v. Ram Swarup Jain, which held that a lease requiring registration is void unless so created. The Court also approved the approach in Jagat Taran Beery v. Sardar Sant Singh that absence of a registered instrument excludes application of the yearly-lease presumption.

rule.if: eviction_appeal_challenges_notice and oral_tenancy and manufacturing_purpose_claimed and no_registered_lease and notice_receipt_undisputed

predicates.eviction_appeal_challenges_notice: A party appealing an eviction decision challenges the termination notice as legally insufficient.
predicates.oral_tenancy: The tenancy was created by an oral agreement.
predicates.manufacturing_purpose_claimed: The tenant asserts that the premises were leased for a manufacturing purpose.
predicates.no_registered_lease: No registered instrument created a lease for a year or longer, or one reserving yearly rent.
predicates.notice_receipt_undisputed: The tenant does not dispute receiving the termination notice.
predicates.short_notice_challenge_fails: The challenge that the termination notice was too short fails.

issues.definition: When an eviction appeal challenges a termination notice based on an asserted manufacturing tenancy, the tenancy was oral without a registered instrument, and receipt of the notice is undisputed, the challenge fails.
